summary:
Federal agencies are proceeding with plans affecting D.C. landmarks, including Park Service contracts related to a golf course project and a Kennedy Center closure that has generated legal disputes over authority and congressional oversight. Meanwhile, statehood advocates are pointing to these federal interventions as examples of why D.C. needs greater local control, with at least one senator pledging to prioritize statehood legislation.

Without statehood, D.C. residents have no voting representation in Congress, and Congress can override any law the District passes.
